;Armed conflict and attacks
*[[Iran–United States relations]]
**[[U.S. President]] [[Donald Trump]] orders 1,500 [[United States Armed Forces|troops]] and several [[Patriot missile]] launchers to the [[Persian Gulf]] as tensions rise with [[Iran]]. [https://www.cbsnews.com/news/trump-to-order-additional-forces-to-middle-east/ (CBS)]
*[[2019 Lyon bomb attack]]
**Multiple people are injured in [[Lyon]], [[France]], by a [[Nail bomb|bomb filled with bolts]].  [https://www.cnn.com/2019/05/24/europe/lyon-blast-intl/index.html (CNN)]
*[[Insurgency in Balochistan]]
**A bombing at a mosque in the Pakistani city of [[Quetta]], the capital of the restive province of [[Balochistan, Pakistan|Balochistan]], kills three people, including the prayer leader, and injures at least 28 worshippers. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2019/05/explosion-targets-mosque-southwestern-pakistans-quetta-190524093711661.html (Al Jazeera)]
*[[War in Afghanistan (2001–2021)]]
**Three people, including a senior [[Muslims|Muslim]] [[Preacher|preacher]], [[Kabul mosque bombing 2019|are killed]] and at least 20 injured after an explosion in a mosque during Friday prayers in the Afghan capital, [[Kabul]]. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2019/05/deadly-explosion-hits-mosque-afghanistan-kabul-190524093958397.html (Al Jazeera)]
*[[2019 Portuguesa, Venezuela prison uprising]]
**At least 23 prisoners are killed during a [[prison riot]] in [[Acarigua]], [[Portuguesa (state)|Portuguesa]], [[Venezuela]]. [http://time.com/5595810/venezuelan-guards-kill-inmates-uprising/ (''TIME'')] [https://www.washingtonpost.com/world/the_americas/rights-group-23-inmates-killed-in-venezuelan-jail-riot/2019/05/24/70d90a54-7e5c-11e9-b1f3-b233fe5811ef_story.html?noredirect=on&utm_term=.7377119fa68a (''Washington Post'')]
;Disasters and accidents
*[[2019 Surat fire]]
**Twenty children die in a fire in [[Surat]], India. [https://www.indiatoday.in/india/story/gujarat-surat-coaching-centre-fire-casualties-injured-fire-department-live-updates-1533860-2019-05-24 (''India Today'')]
*[[2017–2019 eruptions of Mount Agung]]
**[[Mount Agung]] in [[Bali]], [[Indonesia]], erupts. [https://www.abc.net.au/news/2019-05-25/balis-mt-agung-volcano-erupts-forcing-flight-cancellations/11149336 (ABC)]
;Law and crime
*[[Shiregreen child deaths]]
**During a police raid, six children are found unconscious inside a residential property in the [[Shiregreen]] suburb of [[Sheffield]], [[England]]. The eldest two children, aged 13 and 14, subsequently died at [[Sheffield Children's Hospital]]; the other four children remain hospitalised. [https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/uk-england-south-yorkshire-48397021 (BBC News)]
**Two people – a 37-year-old man and a 34-year-old woman – have been arrested under suspicion of murder at the property in Sheffield where six children were found. They remain in police custody. A murder investigation has been opened. [https://www.standard.co.uk/news/uk/six-children-taken-to-hospital-after-serious-incident-in-sheffield-a4150646.html (''Evening Standard'')]
*[[LGBT rights in Taiwan]], [[Legal status of same-sex marriage]]
**Same-sex marriage [[Same-sex marriage in Taiwan|becomes legal]] in [[Taiwan]], making Taiwan the first nation in [[Asia]] to recognize [[same-sex marriage]]. [https://web.archive.org/web/20190517081651/https://www.telegraph.co.uk/news/2019/05/17/taiwan-becomes-first-country-asia-legalise-same-sex-marriage/ (''The Telegraph'')]
*[[LGBT rights in Kenya]]
**The [[High Court of Kenya|High Court]] of [[Kenya]] rules against a bid to strike down Section 162 and 165 of the Kenyan Penal Code, a [[sodomy law]]. The plaintiffs plan to appeal to the [[Court of Appeal of Kenya|Court of Appeal]]. [https://www.nation.co.ke/news/Court-declines-scrap-anti-gay-sex-law/1056-5130052-jqxp7t/ (''Daily Nation'')] [https://www.theguardian.com/world/2019/may/24/kenya-court-upholds-ban-on-gay-sex-in-major-setback-for-campaigners (''The Guardian'')]
*Aftermath of the [[kidnapping of Jayme Closs]]
**In the U.S. state of [[Wisconsin]], Jake Thomas Patterson is sentenced to life in prison for the kidnapping of Jayme Closs and the murders of her parents. [https://www.npr.org/2019/05/24/726803919/wisconsin-man-sentenced-to-2-life-terms-for-kidnapping-teen-murdering-her-parent (NPR)]
*[[Human Life Protection Act]]
**A federal lawsuit is filed to block [[Alabama]]’s abortion ban. [https://abcnews.go.com/Health/wireStory/federal-lawsuit-filed-block-alabamas-abortion-ban-63253763 (ABC News)]
*[[Abortion in the United States by state]], [[Heartbeat bill]]
**The [[List of governors of Missouri|Governor of Missouri]] [[Mike Parson]] signs [[Heartbeat_bill#Missouri|House Bill 126]] into law, effective on August 28, 2019, bans all abortions in the state of [[Missouri]] at or beyond {{nowrap|8 weeks}} of pregnancy, except in cases of medical emergencies. Persons who perform abortion in the state after {{nowrap|8 weeks}} of pregnancy face {{nowrap|5 to 15 years}} in prison. [https://www.cbsnews.com/live-news/missouri-abortion-law-mike-parson-signs-bill-banning-abortions-8-weeks-today-2019-05-24-live-updates/ (CBS News)] [https://www.kansascity.com/news/politics-government/article230790159.html (''The Kansas City Star'')]
*[[Trial of Catalonia independence leaders]]
**The Board of the [[Congress of Deputies]] suspends [[Jordi Turull]], [[Josep Rull]], [[Oriol Junqueras]] and [[Jordi Sànchez]] Catalan leaders elected lawmakers due to they judicial situation. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-spain-politics/spanish-parliament-suspends-jailed-catalan-leaders-rights-as-lawmakers-idUSKCN1SU1BP (Reuters)]

;Politics and elections
*[[2019 European Parliament election]]
**Voters in [[2019 European Parliament election in Ireland|Ireland]] and the [[2019 European Parliament election in the Czech Republic|Czech Republic]] head to the polls to vote for their country's representatives in the [[European Parliament]]. [http://www.europarl.europa.eu/at-your-service/en/be-heard/elections (European Parliament)]
*[[2019 Conservative Party leadership election|2019 UK Conservative Party leadership election]]
**[[Prime Minister of the United Kingdom|United Kingdom Prime Minister]] [[Theresa May]] announces her resignation as leader of the [[Conservative Party (UK)|Conservative Party]], effective June 7. She will remain Prime Minister until a successor is elected. [https://www.theguardian.com/politics/2019/may/24/theresa-may-steps-down-resigns-tory-leader-conservative-brexit (''The Guardian'')]
*The [[United States|U.S.]] [[Supreme Court of the United States|Supreme Court]] temporarily blocks the redrawing of [[Ohio's congressional districts|Ohio]] and [[Michigan's congressional districts|Michigan]] electoral maps while it prepares to rule on whether or not partisan [[Gerrymandering in the United States|gerrymandering]] is constitutional. [[Federal judiciary of the United States|Lower federal courts]] ordered Michigan and Ohio electoral maps to be redrawn before the [[2020 United States presidential election]]. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-usa-court-gerrymandering/us-supreme-court-blocks-redrawing-of-ohio-michigan-electoral-maps-idUSKCN1SU292 (Reuters)] [https://www.latimes.com/politics/la-na-pol-supreme-court-gerrymander-republicans-20190524-story.html (''Los Angeles Times'')]
